title: Trace Sampler Field Notes — 2027-05-15
body:
Summary:
This is a field-oriented writeup from the observability huddle on 2027-05-15. Focus was on the trace-sampler experiment (adaptive per-route probabilistic sampler), dashboarding adjustments to surface effective sample rate, and a short cost telemetry investigation where tokenized span cardinality spiked in prod on 2027-05-13. Notes below include quick standups, experiment observations, immediate mitigations, and next steps.

Participants:
- Priya Patel (notes / lead)
- Ethan Moore (data pipelines / exporter)
- Ana Gomez (runtime instrumentation / SDK)
- Liam Brooks (dashboards / grafana)
- Sofia Ivanov (site reliability / throttles)

Standup snippets (2–3 line each):
- Priya: Ran end-to-end run of adaptive sampler v0.9 against staging traffic profile; saw 22% fewer spans emitted for long-tail routes with negligible change in p99 latency. Preparing a short-run A/B to compare surface-level error rates.
- Ethan: Exporter backpressure surfaced on bursty per-tenant traces; added a 10s queue drain metric to the pipeline to help triage. Working on PR to make exporter retry backoff configurable per pool.
- Ana: SDK change to add route-label normalization rolled out to 5% — confirmed low cardinality benefit; one client had unexpected dynamic route tokens that we need to rewrite on the client-side.
- Liam: Dashboard tile "effective-sample-rate" added to per-route overview. Also created a heatmap that correlates sample rate vs span size to identify expensive spans.
- Sofia: Observed cost telemetry alert firing for span-cardinality delta on 2027-05-13; applied short-term quota bump for the affected org and flagged for root cause.

Deep dive: Adaptive sampler experiment (v0.9)
- Hypothesis: Per-route probabilistic sampling with an adaptive target (targetSpansPerMinute per route) will reduce export cost while preserving signal for high-error routes.
- How v0.9 works (runbook summary):
  - Sample probability p(route) is adjusted every minute based on observed throughput and target budget; routes with low error density get reduced p.
  - A floor probability of 0.01 prevents total dropouts for routes that temporarily look quiet.
  - Integration with KV cache: we propagate the sample decision through the KV cache key so continuation calls keep the same sampling decision.
- Staging results: 18–25% reduction in exported spans across a synthesized traffic profile (heavy tail) with no measurable signal loss for routes labeled critical.
- Concerns discovered:
  - Cold-start routes: routes that appear suddenly have delayed p calibration and can either be over-sampled for a minute or under-sampled if traffic is sporadic. Suggested mitigation: short-term constant p=0.1 for new route fingerprint for first 60s.
  - Downstream tooling expects some minimum span density (alert thresholds assume historical throughput). Need to add sample-aware thresholds.

Cost telemetry incident (2027-05-13) — brief RCA notes
- Symptom: sudden 3.2x increase in span-cardinality metric for org:acme-corp between 03:40–04:10 UTC. Cost alert fired and escalated to SRE.
- Immediate mitigation: manual quota bump and temporary sampling override to 5% for that org.
- Root cause (preliminary): a client-side change concatenated user IDs into route metadata (unbounded cardinality) which passed through instrumentation normalization because tokenization rule missed this pattern.
- Action items from RCA:
  - Add route-label sanitizers to server-side SDK that detect repeated delimiters and clamp token length (Ana) — due 2027-05-22.
  - Create an alert that watches per-org distinct label growth rate and auto-reduce sample rate when cardinality growth > 200%/5m (SRE task, Sofia) — due 2027-05-20.
  - Outreach to customer success to coordinate remediation with Acme (Priya) — done (initial ping), follow-up on 2027-05-16.

Dashboard changes and instrumentation to ship this week
- New tiles merged to staging:
  - effective-sample-rate (per-route, time-series, rolling 1m)
  - sampled-span-size-distribution (bucketed by bytes)
  - per-org-distinct-label-count (delta & rolling window)
- Small UX change: when effective-sample-rate < 0.05 we show a yellow banner on route view explaining "low sampling may affect alert fidelity" with a link to runbook. (Liam to push to prod on 2027-05-19)

Open questions & trade-offs
- How aggressive should auto-throttle be for first-party vs third-party customers? We have different SLAs and need a policy: conservative for enterprise trials, aggressive for free-tier. Proposal: two policy presets (enterprise, best-effort) and one manual override.
- Sample-aware alerting: do we store sampled_count + effective_sample_rate with every alerted metric, or rewrite existing thresholds to ingest sample rate? Storing both increases cardinality; rewriting thresholds is heavy. Prefer storing metadata summary at alert time.

Action items (owner — due)
- Ana: SDK server-side sanitizer + token clamp prototype (2027-05-22)
- Liam: Promote effective-sample-rate tile to prod and add banner copy (2027-05-19)
- Ethan: Exporter backoff PR and queue-drain metric instrumentation (2027-05-21)
- Sofia: Implement per-org cardinality growth alert and auto-reduce sampling webhook (2027-05-20)
- Priya: Coordinate Acme remediation call and capture customer timeline (2027-05-16)

Short notes from playtest run (observability lab)
- When the sampler floor was set to 0.005 we observed a modest regression in error-rate SNR for infrequent auth routes — raised floor to 0.01 while we tune.
- Heatmap shows span-size hotspots are concentrated in three endpoints; plan to instrument those endpoints to capture header-only spans for large requests so we prune payload-heavy spans early.

Next meeting agenda (2027-05-22)
- Review SDK sanitizer alpha and per-route cold-start mitigation telemetry (Ana)
- Cost telemetry alert test results and automation readiness (Sofia & Ethan)
- Quick dashboard walkthrough of sample-aware alerts (Liam)
- Decide policy presets for auto-throttle (Priya)

Notes to self / miscellaneous:
- Put a short blurb in the weekly eng update about "sampler A/B" and expected cost delta so sales ops sees projection.
- Keep an eye on github PR #412 for any exporter contract changes that affect downstream retention flows.

End of field notes.
